_comment: Permission rules the firm has WITHDRAWN. firm-install only ever unions rules into a project's
settings.json, so a project installed from an older version keeps a retired rule forever unless
something removes it. `firm-install --migrate` is that something, and firm-doctor FAILS while a
retired rule is still present — a warning would leave the hole open in every existing project.
The ENFORCED fix is removing Bash(cat:*)/Bash(jq:*) from `allow`: that unconditionally stops the
blanket auto-approval, regardless of anything below. It falls through to the tool-default prompt.
UNVERIFIED SUPPLEMENTAL PROTECTION, not enforced security: .claude/settings.json also adds `deny`
entries (Bash(cat .env*), Bash(cat ~/.ssh/**), etc.) as a second layer. Their pattern syntax was
never confirmed against Claude Code's live permission engine — every existing Bash rule in that
file uses the `Bash(cmd:*)` colon-prefix form, these use a bare-glob form instead, and nothing in
the firm exercises real permission matching (the test suite only checks the rules are present as
JSON strings). Treat them as best-effort, not as proof a matching command will actually be denied.
Even a working deny rule is not a sandbox: `cat -A ~/.ssh/id_rsa`, a pipe through `awk`, or reading
the file from python all sit outside a simple command-prefix pattern. The dev-container and scoped,
read-only credentials are the actual containment; these deny rules are a bonus, not a guarantee.

retired.reason: Read-tool deny rules (Read(./.env), Read(~/.ssh/**), Read(~/.aws/**), Read(~/.codex/auth.json)) bind ONLY the Read tool. An allow-listed `cat` reads straight around every one of them.
retired.replacement: Use the Read tool, which the deny rules actually bind. Ad-hoc `cat` now falls through to the normal permission prompt.

retired.reason: Same read-around as `cat`, aimed at JSON credential stores (~/.claude.json, ~/.codex/auth.json, cloud credential files).
retired.replacement: Read the file with the Read tool. jq on the firm's own ledger artifacts now prompts once rather than being blanket-granted.
